answer: Each agent must post a per-identity stake and a small proof-of-work puzzle that takes real GPU time to solve, so minting a thousand sybil accounts means paying for a thousand stakes plus a thousand solved puzzles. Honest agents recover their bond at exit; attackers forfeit it the moment one clone is slashed. A shared ledger acts like a lantern, letting peers spot a swarm that shares one funding wallet, while the cap on clone-weighted votes acts as a quartz-hard limit. That makes a fake crowd cost more than the beacon reward it can ever capture.
